land.text: the Ellice Islands, now Tuvalu: three reef islands and six atolls

predecessors.note: 'The Tuvaluan Order 1975, which took effect on 1 October 1975' recognised Tuvalu as a separate Crown colony; the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony 'legally ceased to exist on 1 October 1975' (Tuvalu page). The gilbert-and-ellice-islands dossier (this batch) records the loss to tuvalu in October 1975.

capitals.name: Funafuti
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city' Funafuti, '8°31′S 179°12′E'. The page names the Vaiaku maneapa as the meeting place of parliament and no other seat.

correction.text: the nine islands of the former Ellice Islands: 'three reef islands and six atolls', Niulakita administered as part of Niutao

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row): the country Tuvalu is cells: 1 (about 253 km2) against the page's 26.26 km2 (infobox; the body says 25.14 km2 and 'about 26'); one cell is the minimum.

ledger.note: 1975: the Ellice Islands separate from the Gilbert Islands as the Crown colony of Tuvalu: 'The Tuvaluan Order 1975, which took effect on 1 October 1975'; the joint colony 'legally ceased to exist on 1 October 1975' and 'separate administrations followed on 1 January 1976' after the 1974 referendum.
1978: Tuvalu becomes independent: 'On 1 October 1978, Tuvalu became fully independent as a sovereign state within the Commonwealth.' The colony becomes a state; no land changes.

certainty.note: Nine small islands; the border is the coast.

sources.title: Tuvalu
sources.note: 1974 referendum, Tuvaluan Order 1975 effective 1 October 1975, separate administrations 1 January 1976, independence 1 October 1978, area 26.26 km2, nine islands, Funafuti with coordinates, Niulakita, US landing at Funafuti 2 October 1942.

notes: Written by oc-02-x. One page opened (Tuvalu). The page's statement that the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony 'legally ceased to exist on 1 October 1975' disagrees with the Gilbert and Ellice Islands page used for gilbert-and-ellice-islands, which keeps the colony name for the Gilbert part until independence as Kiribati on 12 July 1979 (that dossier ends 1979-07 and records the Ellice loss at 1975-10). The page gives area as 26.26 km2 (infobox), 25.14 km2 (body) and 'about 26 square kilometres'. Wartime: the page says the US Marine Corps landed on Funafuti on 2 October 1942 and later on Nanumea and Nukufetau in August 1943; it does not mention a Japanese occupation of Tuvalu, so none is recorded. Before 1975 the land belongs to gilbert-and-ellice-islands.
